name: Explorers' League
summary: Across Azeroth, the Explorers' League seeks the lost beginnings of the dwarves. King Magni Bronzebeard helped found it, and his brother Brann now leads its work from Ironforge's Hall of Explorers. The League searches far beyond dwarven lands, where its digs often stir conflict.

sections.title: A Shift in Dwarven Purpose
sections.body:
Dwarves in Khaz Modan once devoted their strength to mining, stonework, and engineering. Ancient ruins then pointed to a forgotten bond between dwarves and the mythical titans who created them.

King Magni Bronzebeard wanted to learn his people's origins, so he turned much of dwarven industry toward archaeology. With his brother Brann, Magni founded the Explorers' Guild, now called the Explorers' League. Its members seek relics, lost cities, and signs of their ancient ancestry.

sections.title: The Hall and the Digs
sections.body: The League directs its work from Ironforge's Hall of Explorers. High Explorer Muninn Magellas handles daily affairs while Brann Bronzebeard explores distant lands. Prospectors oversee broad digsites across Khaz Modan and beyond. At Ironband's Excavation in Loch Modan and Whelgar's Excavation in the Wetlands, they uncover vast fossil beds and ancient buildings. Displaced wildlife, troggs, and rival factions seeking buried relics often besiege the prospectors.

sections.title: Frontier Clashes
sections.body: Beyond dwarven lands, the League's expeditions have met fierce resistance. In Kalimdor, blasting at the Bael Modan dig in the southern Barrens drove out the native Stonespire tauren. The work stirred their anger and roused local earth spirits. In the Badlands, League prospectors openly clash with the Dark Iron clan over the vast titan vaults of Uldaman.

faq.answer: The Explorers' League searches for relics and studies the origins of the dwarven race. Based in Ironforge, its members work at digsites across the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor.

King Magni Bronzebeard helped found the League, and his youngest brother, Brann Bronzebeard, leads it. When Brann explores distant lands, High Explorer Muninn Magellas oversees its affairs in Ironforge's Hall of Explorers.

faq.q: Why did King Magni start the League?
faq.answer: King Magni turned much of dwarven industry toward archaeology after underground ruins suggested a mythical heritage tied to the titans. He wanted to discover the beginnings of his people.
Yes. Though most members and leaders are dwarves, other Alliance races join the League. They include adventurous gnomes such as Clopper Wizbang and trusted field assistants across the continents.

faq.q: Why are the tauren fighting the Explorers' League?
faq.answer: Dwarven prospectors at Bael Modan used heavy explosives and displaced the native Stonespire tauren. The blasts devastated their settlement and angered local earth spirits by destroying sacred ground.

faq.q: What is Uldaman and why does the League care about it?
faq.answer: Uldaman is a vast underground titan facility beneath the Badlands. The League sees it as the crown jewel of its research and believes its sealed chambers hold proof of the dwarves' transformation and ancient creation.

angles.text: Each digsite and titan artifact brings dwarves closer to understanding their ancient creators and their departure from stone.
The League's careless use of dynamite in Kalimdor desecrated Stonespire ancestral lands. Its relentless digging often comes at the earth's expense.
The League carries the Alliance banner into remote territories. Its prospectors often need protection from troggs, rival factions, and angry locals.
Dwarven prospectors draw on mining traditions to shore up tunnels, survey strata, and free delicate titan machinery from solid rock.
